summary: SIXTH-G is an SI powered website which addresses the Space Apps Challenge titled "Flame in Freefall" about microgravity combustion. The website aims to check whether a material is safe for missions on Earth, the Moon, Mars and ISS by determining percentage risk for fire occurrence under a variety of environmental conditions. Since fire safety is extremely important in space exploration, Burning Tigers has developed the website.
details:
Two SI models have been trained:

1)The Bayesian Logistic Regression Model is trained on the microgravity combustion experimental datasets that were found on the PSI Database titled "NASA DATA". It is used to determine whether a successful ignition can burn or will go out given the flow speed, the material, and the location (On Earth, the Moon, Mars or inside the ISS). Claude has been used to organize the many PSI datasets into a single one suitable for training the first model. Antigravity has been used to train the first model. A balanced accuracy of 92% has been reached.

2) The second model, which is the LLM Model, has been used to generate simulation videos of flame behavior within 3D Objects, sourced from the 3D resources of NASA. The Model Llama 3.2 : 1 Billion Parameter model generates a video simulation of the provided situation (with reference to official NASA resources) that contains visual insights and graphs from the data and results.

Furthermore, upon entering the site LLM APIs such as the Gemini and ChatGPT APIs were used so that these models are connected to the site, in the generation of specialized insights with regard to the context the user provides, and used as a chat function to allow users to ask questions regarding the analyses insights generated for consulting.

The coding languages Python (for SI training) and HTML (Website Generation) were used. No hardware has been used in the project.

SIXTH -G can help engineers determine the environmental conditions in which risk of fire is minimized. If not taken into account, any potential fire risk on a long duration may pose a technical weakness which can result in damage to humanlife and missions conducted.

The project is authentic as SI has been used responsibly, and in many projects and researchs people have always used the data between earth and ISS which is suitable yet we have used this system and applied it on Mars' and the Moon's environment to provide a new perspective in the insight of this subject. The website uses SI connecting through API passwords to give insight consulting on the subject to introduce the terms in a more simplistic manner and allow people to understand the logic of the subject which will render the user range to enhance the impact of the project even more.

There are several limiting factors for the project. Firstly, there are only a limited amount of experimental data acquired which could be used for SI training. Furthermore, the accuracy of the experiments regarding flame behaviour for the Moon and Mars are limited as there are no suitable experiments physically conducted on these extraterrestrial bodies. Instead, environmental conditions are simulated to emulate these environments, which can only have limited success. So we have regulated the limited datasets by;

1) Omitting the outliers which have misled the SI and deviated the accuracy of simulated experiments on various environmental conditions

2) Omitting data where ignition was not successful and the flow speed was not directly measured.
